107	def merkle_root(tx_ids: list[str]) -> str:
108	    """SHA-256 Merkle root of the given tx ids.
109	
110	    Levels are built by hashing ``sha256(left + right)`` hex-string pairs;
111	    a lone odd node at a level is promoted by pairing it with itself.
112	    Callers normally pass ids already sorted ascending.
113	    """
114	    if not tx_ids:
115	        return EMPTY_MERKLE_ROOT
116	    level = list(tx_ids)
117	    while len(level) > 1:
118	        if len(level) % 2 == 1:
119	            level.append(level[-1])
120	        level = [
121	            sha256_hex((level[i] + level[i + 1]).encode("ascii"))
122	            for i in range(0, len(level), 2)

131	_HEX128_RE = re.compile(r"[0-9a-f]{128}")

153	    """Sibling path from the leaf at ``index`` up to the Merkle root.
154	
155	    Mirrors :func:`merkle_root`: levels hash ``sha256(left + right)`` hex pairs
156	    and a lone odd node is paired with itself. Each returned item has a
157	    ``direction`` ("left" or "right") recording which side the *sibling* sits
158	    on relative to the path node, and the sibling's ``hash``. Items are ordered
159	    from the leaf level toward the root. Raises ValueError for an empty list or
160	    an out-of-range index.

163	        raise ValueError("cannot build a Merkle proof for an empty tree")
164	    if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int):
165	        raise ValueError("index must be an integer")
166	    if index < 0 or index >= len(tx_ids):
167	        raise ValueError("transaction index out of range")
168	
169	    level = list(tx_ids)
170	    position = index
171	    siblings: list[dict] = []
172	    while len(level) > 1:
173	        if len(level) % 2 == 1:
174	            level.append(level[-1])
175	        if position % 2 == 0:
176	            # Path node is the left child; sibling sits on its right.
177	            siblings.append({"direction": "right", "hash": level[position + 1]})
178	        else:

180	            siblings.append({"direction": "left", "hash": level[position - 1]})

183	            for i in range(0, len(level), 2)
184	        ]

432	    ``{account, balance, confirmed_transactions}``, walks the leaf-to-root
433	    ``siblings`` path, and requires the recomputed root to equal both the
434	    proof's ``state_root`` and ``expected_root``, while ``height`` /
435	    ``block_hash`` anchor the tree to the expected confirmed tip. Every
436	    malformed input — a non-64-char lowercase hex hash or anchor, an illegal
437	    direction, an illegal index, a malformed leaf/balance/transaction list, a
438	    path inconsistent with the index, excessive depth — returns False rather
439	    than raising.
440	    """
441	    try:
442	        if not isinstance(proof, dict):
443	            return False
444	        account = proof.get("account")
445	        balance = proof.get("balance")
446	        transactions = proof.get("confirmed_transactions")
447	        index = proof.get("index")
448	        state_root = proof.get("state_root")
449	        height = proof.get("height")
450	        block_hash = proof.get("block_hash")
451	        siblings = proof.get("siblings")

454	            return False

456	            return False

461	        if isinstance(index, bool) or not isinstance(index, int) or index < 0:
462	            return False

466	        else:

468	        if not _is_hex64(state_root):

470	        if not _is_hex64(block_hash) or not _is_hex64(expected_hash):
471	            return False
472	        if not _is_hex64(expected_root):
473	            return False
474	        if not isinstance(siblings, list) or len(siblings) > MAX_MERKLE_DEPTH:
475	            return False
476	
477	        # The leaf is always recomputed from the proof's own triple; a
478	        # client-supplied leaf value is never trusted.
479	        depth = len(siblings)

1	"""Persistent storage: blockchain, pending set and derived indexes (JSON).
2	
3	The whole state is one JSON document written atomically: a uniquely named
4	``.ledger-*`` snapshot is fsynced in the same directory and then promoted over
5	the main file with ``os.replace`` (followed by a directory fsync). Every
6	successful write advances a monotonic ``generation`` recorded in the
7	snapshot. A crash can therefore only leave behind (a) the previous main file
8	or (b) a fully fsynced snapshot that never got renamed — never a torn file.
9	
10	On startup the main file and every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
11	as recovery candidates. When no file exists at all, the unique genesis block
12	is created; otherwise each candidate is strictly validated (JSON, generation,
13	consecutive heights, prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and Merkle
14	roots, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signature, pending-only-at-tip and
15	mempool/chain de-duplication). The valid snapshot with the highest generation
16	wins and is promoted if it is still a temp file; same-generation content
17	conflicts, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise StateRecoveryError
18	with the offending path and reason — a fresh chain is never silently created.
19	
20	One atomic write persists everything: the chain (each block carries its
21	confirm/rollback ``status``), a small ``state`` summary, the mempool
22	(``pending``), candidate fork chains (``forks``, each a full block list
23	anchored at the canonical genesis and keyed by its tip hash), the
24	confirmed-transaction ``index`` and the confirmed ``accounts`` activity.
25	Derived data (index/accounts) is *rebuilt* from the chain on every load and
26	every save — pending blocks are excluded, so a restart never resurrects
27	unconfirmed transactions into balances. Persisted fork candidates are
28	re-validated on startup and invalid ones are dropped, while canonical-chain
29	invalidity remains fatal. Each surviving sync record carries the tip summary
30	(height/length/status) frozen at reception; a persisted frozen summary that
31	disagrees with the re-resolved candidate invalidates the record, while a
32	snapshot predating the feature is repaired from its candidate. Persisted sync
33	records are re-verified on restart:
34	records still unexpired whose source stays active and unexpired survive;
35	records whose own deadline elapsed or whose source is unknown/revoked/
36	registry-expired while the process was down are pruned (their non-adopted
37	forks removed; an adopted tip never changes the canonical chain) and each
38	gets exactly one sync_expired audit event backfilled after the durable
39	history, persisted in one atomic write. The backfill deduplicates only
40	within the record's current lifecycle (a durable sync_expired newer than
41	the key's latest sync_received), so a reused (source, request_id) key's
42	new lifecycle is always audited even when every field matches a previous
43	lifecycle's event. Other staleness (a dangling
44	tip or a content-fingerprint mismatch) is a silent prune with no event.
45	A re-entrant lock serializes all updates, and a class-wide recovery lock
46	serializes startup scans against in-flight writes.
47	"""

127	    re-parsed/re-serialized approximation of it.

340	    def load(self) -> None:
341	        """Recover state from disk on startup.
342	
343	        The main file *and* every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
344	        as recovery candidates. When none exist at all, the unique genesis
345	        block is created (the established first-start convention); otherwise
346	        every candidate is strictly validated and the valid snapshot with the
347	        highest generation wins. A winning temp snapshot is atomically
348	        promoted over the main file and every judged-older or residual
349	        candidate is removed. Same-generation snapshots with conflicting
350	        content, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise
351	        StateRecoveryError — a fresh chain is never silently created.
352	        """
353	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or "."
354	        with self._recovery_lock:
355	            candidates = self._discover_candidates(directory)
356	            if not candidates:
357	                os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
358	                self.chain = [self.create_genesis()]
359	                self.pending = {}
360	                self.forks = {}
361	                self.syncs = {}
362	                self.attested_syncs = {}
363	                self.trust_sources = {}
364	                self.allowlist = {}
365	                self.audit_events = []
366	                self.audit_checkpoint = audit.make_checkpoint([])
367	                # A brand-new node mints its version 1 checkpoint key; the
368	                # first signer is activated at event 0 (the empty log).
369	                self.audit_signer = self._make_audit_signer(1, 0)
370	                self.audit_signer_history = [self._public_signer_entry(self.audit_signer)]
371	                self.generation = 0
372	                self.rebuild_derived()
373	                self.save()
374	                return
375	
376	            valid: list[tuple] = []
377	            errors: list[StateRecoveryError] = []
378	            for candidate in candidates:
379	                try:
380	                    data = self._read_candidate(candidate)
381	                    parsed = self._parse_snapshot(candidate, data)
382	                except StateRecoveryError as exc:
383	                    errors.append(exc)
384	                    continue
385	                # parsed = (chain, pending, generation, forks, initial_balance,
386	                #           syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
387	                #           expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair,
388	                #           signer_state, recorded_state_root, attested_syncs,
389	                #           attested_expired_records)
390	                valid.append(
391	                    (
392	                        parsed[2],
393	                        candidate,
394	                        parsed[0],
395	                        parsed[1],
396	                        parsed[3],
397	                        parsed[4],
398	                        parsed[5],
399	                        parsed[6],
400	                        parsed[7],
401	                        parsed[8],
402	                        parsed[9],
403	                        parsed[10],
404	                        parsed[11],
405	                        parsed[12],
406	                        parsed[13],
407	                        parsed[14],
408	                        parsed[15],
409	                    )
410	                )
411	
412	            if not valid:
413	                details = "; ".join(f"{exc.path} ({exc.reason})" for exc in errors)
414	                raise StateRecoveryError(
415	                    directory, f"no valid snapshot candidate found: {details}"
416	                )
417	
418	            max_generation = max(item[0] for item in valid)
419	            top = [item for item in valid if item[0] == max_generation]
420	            # item layout: (generation, path, chain, pending, forks,
421	            # initial_balance, syncs, trust_sources, allowlist, audit_events,
422	            # expired_records, audit_checkpoint, audit_repair, signer_state,
423	            # recorded_state_root, attested_syncs, attested_expired_records)
424	            reference = self._canonical_view(
425	                top[0][2],
426	                top[0][3],
427	                top[0][4],
428	                top[0][6],
429	                top[0][7],
430	                top[0][8],
431	                top[0][9],
432	                top[0][5],
433	                top[0][11],
434	                top[0][13][1],
435	                top[0][14],
436	                top[0][15],
437	            )
438	            for item in top[1:]:
439	                if (
440	                    self._canonical_view(
441	                        item[2],
442	                        item[3],
443	                        item[4],
444	                        item[6],
445	                        item[7],
446	                        item[8],
447	                        item[9],
448	                        item[5],
449	                        item[11],
450	                        item[13][1],
451	                        item[14],
452	                        item[15],
453	                    )
454	                    != reference
455	                ):
456	                    paths = " vs ".join(item[1] for item in top)
457	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
458	                        directory,
459	                        f"conflicting snapshots at generation {max_generation}: {paths}",
460	                    )
461	
462	            # Identical same-generation snapshots: keep the main file when it
463	            # is one of them, avoiding a pointless promotion cycle.
464	            main_abs = os.path.abspath(self.path)
465	            winner = top[0]
466	            for item in top:
467	                if os.path.abspath(item[1]) == main_abs:
468	                    winner = item
469	                    break
470	            (
471	                generation,
472	                winner_path,
473	                chain,
474	                pending,
475	                forks,
476	                winner_init_balance,
477	                syncs,
478	                trust_sources,
479	                allowlist,
480	                audit_events,
481	                expired_records,
482	                audit_checkpoint,
483	                audit_repair,
484	                signer_state,
485	                recorded_state_root,
486	                attested_syncs,
487	                attested_expired_records,
488	            ) = winner
489	
490	            # The single winning snapshot is the only one whose recorded
491	            # account-state root is recomputed and pinned, after conflict
492	            # detection. A mismatch is fatal corruption, never silently
493	            # rewritten; a pre-feature snapshot (no state_root) is accepted.
494	            if recorded_state_root is not None:
495	                winner_endowment = (
496	                    winner_init_balance
497	                    if winner_init_balance is not None
498	                    else (
499	                        self.initial_balance
500	                        if self.initial_balance is not None
501	                        else DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE
502	                    )
503	                )
504	                recomputed_state_root, _ = self.state_root_for(
505	                    chain, winner_endowment
506	                )
507	                if recomputed_state_root != recorded_state_root:
508	                    raise StateRecoveryError(
509	                        winner_path,
510	                        "state.state_root does not match the recomputed "
511	                        "account state",
512	                    )
513	
514	            if os.path.abspath(winner_path) != main_abs:
515	                # The newest durable state only ever made it to a temp
516	                # snapshot (a crash interrupted the promotion): promote it.
517	                os.replace(winner_path, self.path)
518	                self._fsync_dir(directory)
519	
520	            # Reconcile records that expired or lost authorization while the
521	            # process was down, once, on the single winning snapshot: append
522	            # deduplicated sync_expired events with ids continuing after the
523	            # durable history. Doing this after same-generation conflict
524	            # detection keeps that comparison based on durable content (the
525	            # backfill carries a current timestamp).
526	            backfilled = self._backfill_expired_events(
527	                audit_events, expired_records, attested_expired_records
528	            )
529	            # A snapshot written before audit hash chaining carries no links;
530	            # expiry backfill events are likewise appended without hashes. In
531	            # both cases the single winning snapshot's log is (re)linked here:
532	            # renumbering dense ids and recomputing reproduces every already
533	            # validated link byte-for-byte and completes the new tail. A
534	            # present-but-wrong chain never reaches this point —
535	            # _parse_snapshot rejects it with StateRecoveryError.
536	            if audit_repair or backfilled:
537	                audit_events = audit.link_events(audit_events)
538	            audit_checkpoint = audit.make_checkpoint(audit_events)
539	
540	            # A pre-checkpoint-auth snapshot carries no signer at all: mint
541	            # its version 1 key once, here, on the unique winner (the
542	            # same-generation conflict comparison above already ran on the
543	            # durable candidates, exactly as for the hash-chain repair). The
544	            # new key is persisted atomically together with the (possibly
545	            # relinked) log and checkpoint in the single save() below.
546	            audit_signer, signer_history, signer_migration = signer_state
547	            if signer_migration:
548	                audit_signer = self._make_audit_signer(1, 0)
549	                signer_history = [self._public_signer_entry(audit_signer)]
550	
551	            self.chain = chain
552	            self.pending = pending
553	            self.forks = forks
554	            self.syncs = syncs
555	            self.attested_syncs = attested_syncs
556	            self.trust_sources = trust_sources
557	            self.allowlist = allowlist
558	            self.audit_events = audit_events
559	            self.audit_checkpoint = audit_checkpoint
560	            self.audit_signer = audit_signer
561	            self.audit_signer_history = signer_history
562	            self.generation = generation
563	            # Prefer the endowment recorded by the writer; fall back to the
564	            # value this instance was constructed with, and finally to the
565	            # service default, so older snapshots without the field still
566	            # validate fork replays against the configured endowment.
567	            if winner_init_balance is not None:
568	                self.initial_balance = winner_init_balance
569	            self.rebuild_derived()
570	            self._cleanup_candidates(directory)
571	            # Persist the reconciled state (pruned records/forks + backfilled
572	            # events + legacy hash-chain completion + signer migration)
573	            # atomically so the next restart never re-derives or duplicates
574	            # anything; with nothing to reconcile no write happens and the
575	            # recovered generation is kept byte-for-byte.
576	            if backfilled or audit_repair or signer_migration:
577	                self.save()

579	    def _discover_candidates(self, directory: str) -> list[str]:
580	        """List the main file and sibling .ledger-* snapshots (if any)."""
581	        candidates: list[str] = []
582	        if os.path.exists(self.path):
583	            candidates.append(self.path)
584	        try:
585	            names = sorted(os.listdir(directory))
586	        except OSError:
587	            return candidates
588	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
589	        for name in names:
590	            if name == main_name or not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX):
591	                continue
592	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
593	            if os.path.isfile(full):
594	                candidates.append(full)
595	        return candidates

597	    @staticmethod
598	    def _canonical_view(
599	        chain: list[Block],
600	        pending: dict[str, Transaction],
601	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
602	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] | None = None,
603	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
604	        allowlist: dict[str, int] | None = None,
605	        audit_events: list[dict] | None = None,
606	        initial_balance: int | None = None,
607	        audit_checkpoint: dict | None = None,
608	        audit_signer_history: list[dict] | None = None,
609	        state_root: str | None = None,
610	        attested_syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] | None = None,
611	    ) -> str:
612	        """Order-independent canonical content hash for conflict detection.
613	
614	        The recorded ``initial_balance`` is part of the authoritative view: two
615	        same-generation snapshots with identical chains but a different
616	        endowment describe a different replay judgment and must conflict. The
617	        audit checkpoint participates too: two same-generation snapshots with
618	        the same events but a different log head disagree about the audited
619	        state and must conflict. The audit signer history (version, public key,
620	        activation event) participates as well, so a checkpoint key that
621	        differs between two same-generation snapshots is a conflict. The
622	        recorded account-state root participates too: a twin carrying a
623	        different ``state_root`` describes a different confirmed state and is
624	        a conflict rather than a quietly accepted alternative. The attested
625	        sync table (with its frozen key/version/signature/signed form) is its
626	        own section so it participates independently of plain syncs.
627	        """
628	        sync_records = [
629	            {
630	                "source": key[0],
631	                "request_id": key[1],
632	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
633	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
634	                "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
635	                "height": rec.get("height"),
636	                "length": rec.get("length"),
637	                "status": rec.get("status"),
638	                # A range delivery's {anchor, blocks} payload participates in
639	                # conflict detection: same-generation snapshots disagreeing
640	                # about the delivered increment are a conflict.
641	                "range": rec.get("range"),
642	            }
643	            for key, rec in sorted((syncs or {}).items())
644	        ]
645	        attested_records = [
646	            {
647	                "source": key[0],
648	                "request_id": key[1],
649	                "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
650	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
651	                "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
652	                "height": rec.get("height"),
653	                "length": rec.get("length"),
654	                "status": rec.get("status"),
655	                # The frozen attestation participates verbatim: a twin
656	                # disagreeing about the signing key, version, signature or
657	                # signed candidate form is a conflict.
658	                "attested": rec.get("attested"),
659	            }
660	            for key, rec in sorted((attested_syncs or {}).items())
661	        ]
662	        trust_records = [
663	            {"source": source, **rec}
664	            for source, rec in sorted((trust_sources or {}).items())
665	        ]
666	        return json.dumps(
667	            {
668	                "initial_balance": initial_balance,
669	                "chain": [block.to_dict() for block in chain],
670	                "pending": [pending[tx_id].to_dict() for tx_id in sorted(pending)],
671	                "forks": [
672	                    [block.to_dict() for block in forks[tip]]
673	                    for tip in sorted(forks)
674	                ],
675	                "syncs": sync_records,
676	                "attested_syncs": attested_records,
677	                "trust_sources": trust_records,
678	                "allowlist": dict(sorted((allowlist or {}).items())),
679	                "audit_events": audit_events or [],
680	                "audit_checkpoint": audit_checkpoint
681	                or {"event_id": 0, "event_hash": "0" * 64},
682	                "audit_signer_history": audit_signer_history or [],
683	                "state_root": state_root,
684	            },
685	            sort_keys=True,
686	            ensure_ascii=False,
687	        )
688	
689	    def _cleanup_candidates(self, directory: str) -> None:
690	        """Remove every residual .ledger-* snapshot next to the main file.
691	
692	        After recovery these are by definition unusable leftovers: older
693	        generations, an identical post-promotion residue, or a partially
694	        written (invalid) file. The promoted/main state is never touched.
695	        """
696	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
697	        for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
698	            if not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX) or name == main_name:
699	                continue
700	            full = os.path.join(directory, name)
701	            try:
702	                if os.path.isfile(full) or os.path.islink(full):
703	                    os.unlink(full)
704	            except OSError:
705	                pass
706	        self._fsync_dir(directory)

708	    @staticmethod
709	    def _read_candidate(path: str) -> dict:
710	        """Read and JSON-decode one snapshot file.
711	
712	        Any I/O or JSON failure becomes a StateRecoveryError carrying the
713	        offending path, never a silent fall-back.
714	        """
715	        try:
716	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
717	                data = json.load(fh)
718	        except OSError as exc:
719	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"cannot read file: {exc}") from exc
720	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
721	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"invalid JSON: {exc}") from exc
722	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
723	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "snapshot root must be a JSON object")
724	        return data

726	    def _parse_snapshot(
727	        self, path: str, data: dict
728	    ) -> tuple[
729	        list[Block],
730	        dict[str, Transaction],
731	        int,
732	        dict[str, list[Block]],
733	        int | None,
734	        dict[tuple[str, str], dict],
735	        dict[str, dict],
736	        dict[str, int],
737	        list[dict],
738	        list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
739	        dict,
740	        bool,
741	        tuple[dict | None, list[dict], bool],
742	        str | None,
743	    ]:
744	        """Strictly validate one decoded snapshot.
745	
746	        Checks the persisted generation, consecutive heights, prev_hash
747	        linkage, recomputed block hashes, recomputed Merkle roots, every
748	        transaction's tx_id and Ed25519 signature, the pending-only-at-tip
749	        rule, and de-duplication between mempool and chain. Returns the parsed
750	        chain, mempool, generation, candidate forks and the recorded initial
751	        balance. Raises StateRecoveryError on the first defect, with ``path``
752	        identifying the candidate.
753	        """
754	        def fail(reason: str) -> None:
755	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, reason)
756	
757	        chain_raw = data.get("chain")
758	        if not isinstance(chain_raw, list) or not chain_raw:
759	            fail("snapshot must contain a non-empty chain")
760	
761	        state = data.get("state")
762	        # A pre-state-section snapshot is accepted: the chain itself is fully
763	        # self-verifying below. A present non-object section is corruption.
764	        if state is None:
765	            state = {}
766	        if not isinstance(state, dict):
767	            fail("invalid 'state' section: must be a JSON object")
768	        generation = state.get("generation", 0)
769	        # bool is an int subclass; reject it explicitly along with negatives.
770	        if isinstance(generation, bool) or not isinstance(generation, int) or generation < 0:
771	            fail("state.generation must be a non-negative integer")
772	        # Schema version gating the one-time pre-checkpoint-auth migration: a
773	        # snapshot written by current code always carries state.version >= 9,
774	        # so a present signer section is mandatory there; only a snapshot whose
775	        # version explicitly predates 9 may lack the signer sections at all.
776	        state_version = state.get("version")
777	        if state_version is not None and (
778	            isinstance(state_version, bool)
779	            or not isinstance(state_version, int)
780	            or state_version < 1
781	        ):
782	            fail("state.version must be a positive integer")
783	        initial_balance = state.get("initial_balance")
784	        if initial_balance is not None and (
785	            isinstance(initial_balance, bool)
786	            or not isinstance(initial_balance, int)
787	            or initial_balance <= 0
788	        ):
789	            fail("state.initial_balance must be a positive integer")
790	        recorded_state_root = state.get("state_root")
791	        if recorded_state_root is not None and not crypto.is_hex64(
792	            recorded_state_root
793	        ):
794	            fail("state.state_root must be 64 lowercase hex characters")
795	
796	        chain: list[Block] = []
797	        seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
798	        for i, block_raw in enumerate(chain_raw):
799	            if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
800	                fail(f"block at position {i} is not a JSON object")
801	            try:
802	                block = Block.from_dict(block_raw)
803	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
804	                fail(f"block {i} is malformed: {exc}")
805	            if block.height != i:
806	                fail(
807	                    f"block at position {i} has non-consecutive height "
808	                    f"{block.height}"
809	                )
810	            expected_prev = GENESIS_PREV_HASH if i == 0 else chain[i - 1].block_hash
811	            if block.prev_hash != expected_prev:
812	                fail(f"block {block.height} has a mismatched prev_hash")
813	            if block.status not in (STATUS_PENDING, STATUS_CONFIRMED):
814	                fail(f"block {block.height} has unknown status {block.status!r}")
815	            if i == 0 and (
816	                block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.transactions
817	            ):
818	                fail("genesis block must be confirmed and carry no transactions")
819	            # Pending blocks may only sit at the chain tip.
820	            if i < len(chain_raw) - 1 and block.status == STATUS_PENDING:
821	                fail(f"pending block {block.height} is not the chain tip")
822	
823	            # Validate every transaction: stored tx_id, recomputed tx_id and
824	            # the Ed25519 signature.
825	            tx_ids: list[str] = []
826	            txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
827	            if not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
828	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions must be a list")
829	            for j, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
830	                self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
831	                stored_tx_id = txs_raw[j].get("tx_id") if isinstance(txs_raw[j], dict) else None
832	                if stored_tx_id != tx.tx_id:
833	                    fail(
834	                        f"transaction in block {block.height} has a mismatched "
835	                        f"tx_id (stored {stored_tx_id!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
836	                    )
837	                if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
838	                    fail(
839	                        f"duplicate transaction {tx.tx_id} in block "
840	                        f"{block.height}"
841	                    )
842	                seen_tx_ids.add(tx.tx_id)
843	                tx_ids.append(tx.tx_id)
844	            # Blocks store transactions in ascending tx_id order.
845	            if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
846	                fail(f"block {block.height} transactions are not tx_id sorted")
847	
848	            recomputed_merkle = crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids)
849	            if recomputed_merkle != block.merkle_root:
850	                fail(f"block {block.height} Merkle root mismatch")
851	            recomputed_hash = compute_block_hash(
852	                block.height, block.prev_hash, block.merkle_root
853	            )
854	            if recomputed_hash != block.block_hash:
855	                fail(f"block {block.height} block_hash mismatch")
856	            chain.append(block)
857	
858	        # Mempool: well-formed, no internal duplicates, never overlapping the
859	        # chain (neither confirmed nor pending-block transactions).
860	        pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
861	        pending_raw = data.get("pending", [])
862	        if not isinstance(pending_raw, list):
863	            fail("'pending' must be a list")
864	        for tx_raw in pending_raw:
865	            if not isinstance(tx_raw, dict):
866	                fail("pending entry is not a JSON object")
867	            try:
868	                tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
869	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
870	                fail(f"pending transaction is malformed: {exc}")
871	            self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
872	            if tx_raw.get("tx_id") != tx.tx_id:
873	                fail(
874	                    f"pending transaction has a mismatched tx_id (stored "
875	                    f"{tx_raw.get('tx_id')!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
876	                )
877	            if tx.tx_id in pending:
878	                fail(f"duplicate pending transaction {tx.tx_id} in mempool")
879	            if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
880	                fail(
881	                    f"pending transaction {tx.tx_id} already exists in a block"
882	                )
883	            pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
884	
885	        # Cross-check the persisted tip summary against the chain tail.
886	        tip = chain[-1]
887	        if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
888	            fail("state.height does not match the chain tip")
889	        if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
890	            fail("state.tip_hash does not match the chain tip")
891	        if (
892	            state.get("tip_status") is not None
893	            and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
894	        ):
895	            fail("state.tip_status does not match the chain tip")
896	
897	        # The recorded endowment is the *only* balance-replay parameter for the
898	        # persisted fork candidates: revalidation below must use it rather than
899	        # this instance's constructor argument, so starting with a different
900	        # --initial-balance can never change a fork's legality. Only a legacy
901	        # snapshot that records no endowment falls back to the configured (then
902	        # the default) value; every snapshot written by current code records it.
903	        replay_endowment = initial_balance
904	        if replay_endowment is None:
905	            replay_endowment = (

971	            syncs,

973	            allowlist,

984	    @staticmethod
985	    def _assess_audit_chain(
986	        data: dict, audit_events: list[dict], path: str
987	    ) -> tuple[dict, bool]:
988	        """Validate the persisted audit hash chain and checkpoint.
989	
990	        Returns ``(checkpoint, needs_repair)``. Three cases:
991	
992	        * a current snapshot with complete hash links: every dense id,
993	          prev_hash link and event_hash is recomputed and the persisted
994	          ``audit_checkpoint`` must pin the exact log head — any mismatch is
995	          snapshot corruption and fails recovery;
996	        * a legacy snapshot predating hash chaining (no link fields, no
997	          checkpoint, or a checkpoint-less section): accepted for a one-time
998	          repair performed by load() on the unique winner; the checkpoint
999	          returned here is the would-be head so same-generation conflict
1000	          comparison stays content-based;
1001	        * a partially linked log or a present-but-mismatched checkpoint/link:
1002	          corruption, never silently repaired.
1003	        """
1004	        linked_flags = [
1005	            isinstance(event, dict)
1006	            and ("prev_hash" in event or "event_hash" in event)
1007	            for event in audit_events
1008	        ]
1009	        any_linked = any(linked_flags)
1010	        all_linked = all(linked_flags)
1011	        checkpoint_raw = data.get("audit_checkpoint")
1012	        if any_linked and not all_linked:
1013	            raise StateRecoveryError(
1014	                path, "audit log is only partially hash-linked"
1015	            )
1016	        if all_linked and (audit_events or checkpoint_raw is not None):
1017	            # A linked log (or an empty log already carrying a checkpoint) is
1018	            # strictly verified: links recompute and the checkpoint must pin
1019	            # the exact log head.
1020	            try:
1021	                audit.validate_event_chain(audit_events)
1022	            except audit.AuditChainError as exc:
1023	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, exc.reason) from exc
1024	            if checkpoint_raw is None:
1025	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1026	                    path, "hash-linked audit log is missing audit_checkpoint"
1027	                )
1028	            try:
1029	                audit.validate_checkpoint(checkpoint_raw, audit_events)
1030	            except audit.AuditChainError as exc:
1031	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, exc.reason) from exc
1032	            return dict(checkpoint_raw), False
1033	        # Legacy unlinked log (including a pre-feature empty log with no
1034	        # checkpoint). A present checkpoint is inconsistent with an unlinked
1035	        # log: treat as corruption rather than silently ignoring it.
1036	        if checkpoint_raw is not None:
1037	            raise StateRecoveryError(
1038	                path, "audit_checkpoint present on an unlinked audit log"
1039	            )
1040	        linked = audit.link_events(audit_events)
1041	        return audit.make_checkpoint(linked), True

1043	    def _parse_persisted_audit_signer(
1044	        self,
1045	        state: dict,
1046	        chain: list[Block],
1047	        audit_events: list[dict],
1048	        audit_checkpoint: dict,
1049	        path: str,
1050	        state_version: int | None,
1051	    ) -> tuple[dict | None, list[dict], bool]:

1053	
1054	        Returns ``(current_signer, history, needs_migration)``. The one-time
1055	        migration that mints a version 1 key is allowed *only* for a snapshot
1056	        whose ``state.version`` explicitly predates 9 and which carries neither
1057	        an ``audit_signer`` nor an ``audit_signer_history`` section. When the
1058	        version is absent (older than the version field itself is not a
1059	        claim current code ever writes) or is 9+, either section missing —
1060	        including exactly one of the two — is corruption and fails recovery;
1061	        the snapshot is never silently reset to version 1.
1062	
1063	        A present signer section is strictly verified: the stored seed must
1064	        derive the stored public key, the history versions must be dense from
1065	        1 with the first activated at event 0, later activation ids must be
1066	        strictly ascending and never past the checkpoint, the current record
1067	        must equal the latest history entry, every version past 1 must be
1068	        activated by an ``audit_signer_rotated`` event whose id, version and
1069	        public key match, no orphan rotation events may exist, and a signature
1070	        produced by the stored key over the current checkpoint must verify
1071	        under its public key. Any defect fails recovery.
1072	        """
1073	
1074	        def fail(reason: str) -> None:
1075	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, reason)
1076	
1077	        raw = state.get("audit_signer")
1078	        history_raw = state.get("audit_signer_history")
1079	        if raw is None or history_raw is None:
1080	            # The two sections are a single unit on every current snapshot.
1081	            # Only an explicitly old-version snapshot (state.version < 9) may
1082	            # predate both; anything else is corruption, never a reset.
1083	            if raw is None and history_raw is not None:
1084	                fail("audit_signer_history present without an audit_signer")
1085	            if history_raw is None and raw is not None:
1086	                fail("audit_signer present without an audit_signer_history")
1087	            if state_version is not None and state_version < STATE_VERSION:
1088	                return None, [], True
1089	            if state_version is None:
1090	                fail(
1091	                    "snapshot without a state.version is missing both "
1092	                    "audit_signer and audit_signer_history"
1093	                )
1094	            fail(
1095	                f"snapshot at state.version {state_version} is missing both "
1096	                "audit_signer and audit_signer_history"
1097	            )
1098	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
1099	            fail("state.audit_signer must be an object")
1100	        version = raw.get("version")
1101	        private_key = raw.get("private_key")
1102	        public_key = raw.get("public_key")
1103	        activated = raw.get("activated_event_id")
1104	        if (
1105	            isinstance(version, bool)
1106	            or not isinstance(version, int)
1107	            or version < 1
1108	        ):
1109	            fail("audit_signer.version must be a positive integer")
1110	        if not crypto.is_hex64(private_key):
1111	            fail("audit_signer.private_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
1112	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
1113	            fail("audit_signer.public_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
1114	        if crypto.derive_public_key(private_key) != public_key:
1115	            fail("audit_signer private_key does not derive its public_key")
1116	        if isinstance(activated, bool) or not isinstance(activated, int) or activated < 0:
1117	            fail("audit_signer.activated_event_id must be a non-negative integer")
1118	        if not isinstance(history_raw, list) or not history_raw:
1119	            fail("state.audit_signer_history must be a non-empty list")
1120	        history: list[dict] = []
1121	        for position, entry in enumerate(history_raw):
1122	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
1123	                fail("audit_signer_history entry must be an object")
1124	            h_version = entry.get("version")
1125	            h_public = entry.get("public_key")
1126	            h_activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
1127	            if (
1128	                isinstance(h_version, bool)
1129	                or not isinstance(h_version, int)
1130	                or h_version != position + 1
1131	            ):
1132	                fail("audit_signer_history versions must be dense from 1")
1133	            if not crypto.is_hex64(h_public):
1134	                fail("audit_signer_history public_key must be 64 lowercase hex chars")
1135	            if (
1136	                isinstance(h_activated, bool)
1137	                or not isinstance(h_activated, int)
1138	                or h_activated < 0
1139	            ):
1140	                fail("audit_signer_history activated_event_id must be non-negative")
1141	            if position == 0 and h_activated != 0:
1142	                fail("the first audit signer must be activated at event 0")
1143	            if position > 0 and h_activated <= history[-1]["activated_event_id"]:
1144	                fail("audit signer activation ids must be strictly ascending")

1146	                {
1147	                    "version": h_version,
1148	                    "public_key": h_public,
1149	                    "activated_event_id": h_activated,
1150	                }
1151	            )
1152	        latest = history[-1]
1153	        if (
1154	            version != latest["version"]
1155	            or public_key != latest["public_key"]
1156	            or activated != latest["activated_event_id"]
1157	        ):

1178	                event.get("version") != entry["version"]

1180	            ):

1182	                    f"audit_signer_rotated event {event['event_id']} does not "
1183	                    "match the signer history"
1184	                )

1186	            fail("orphan audit_signer_rotated event with no signer history entry")

1189	        # signature produced by the stored seed must verify under its public

1191	        signature = audit.sign_checkpoint_auth(
1192	            private_key,
1193	            chain[0].block_hash,
1194	            audit_checkpoint,
1195	            version,
1196	        )
1197	        if not signature or not audit.verify_checkpoint_auth(
1198	            public_key,
1199	            chain[0].block_hash,
1200	            audit_checkpoint,
1201	            version,
1202	            signature,
1203	        ):
1204	            fail("audit checkpoint signer failed signature re-verification")

1206	        current = {
1207	            "version": version,
1208	            "private_key": private_key,
1209	            "public_key": public_key,
1210	            "activated_event_id": activated,
1211	        }

1214	    @staticmethod
1215	    def _backfill_expired_events(
1216	        audit_events: list[dict],
1217	        expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
1218	        attested_expired_records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]] | None = None,
1219	    ) -> int:
1220	        """Append one sync_expired event per down-time-expired sync record.
1221	
1222	        Mirrors the runtime sweep exactly: records are processed in
1223	        ``(source, request_id)`` order, each gets a dense event_id continuing
1224	        after the durable history, and every *lifecycle removal* gets its own
1225	        event. Deduplication is lifecycle-aware, never identity-based across
1226	        lifecycles: a durable sync_expired covers the persisted record only
1227	        when it sits after the latest sync_received for the same
1228	        ``(source, request_id)`` key — i.e. it belongs to the record's
1229	        current lifecycle (the crash-interrupted-cleanup case). An expiry
1230	        event from an *earlier* lifecycle of a reused key never suppresses
1231	        the new lifecycle's event, even when source, request_id, tip_hash
1232	        and expires_at are all identical.
1233	
1234	        Plain and attested deliveries are separate namespaces: they are
1235	        matched independently against durable events (an attested durable
1236	        event carries ``mode:"attested"``), and backfilled attested events
1237	        carry that mode while plain backfilled events keep the historical
1238	        shape with no mode. Returns the number of events appended. Mutates
1239	        ``audit_events`` in place.
1240	        """
1241	        attested_expired_records = attested_expired_records or []
1242	
1243	        def event_mode(event: dict) -> str:
1244	            mode = event.get("mode")
1245	            return mode if mode == SYNC_MODE_ATTESTED else SYNC_MODE_PLAIN
1246	
1247	        # Position of the latest sync_received per (mode, source, request_id):
1248	        # it opens the lifecycle every later event of that key belongs to.
1249	        last_received: dict[tuple[object, object, object], int] = {}
1250	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
1251	            if event.get("kind") == EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED:
1252	                last_received[
1253	                    (
1254	                        event_mode(event),
1255	                        event.get("source"),
1256	                        event.get("request_id"),
1257	                    )
1258	                ] = index
1259	        # Identities already expired *within their current lifecycle*.
1260	        covered: dict[str, set[tuple[object, object, object]]] = {
1261	            SYNC_MODE_PLAIN: set(),
1262	            SYNC_MODE_ATTESTED: set(),
1263	        }
1264	        for index, event in enumerate(audit_events):
1265	            if event.get("kind") != EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED:
1266	                continue
1267	            mode = event_mode(event)
1268	            key = (mode, event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"))
1269	            if index > last_received.get(key, -1):
1270	                covered[mode].add((event.get("source"), event.get("request_id"),
1271	                                   event.get("tip_hash")))
1272	
1273	        def append_expiry(
1274	            mode: str,
1275	            records: list[tuple[str, str, dict]],
1276	        ) -> int:
1277	            count = 0
1278	            for source, request_id, rec in sorted(
1279	                records, key=lambda item: (item[0], item[1])
1280	            ):
1281	                identity = (source, request_id, rec["tip_hash"])
1282	                if identity in covered[mode]:
1283	                    continue
1284	                event = {
1285	                    "event_id": len(audit_events) + 1,
1286	                    "kind": EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
1287	                    "at": time.time(),
1288	                    "source": source,
1289	                    "request_id": request_id,
1290	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
1291	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
1292	                }
1293	                if mode == SYNC_MODE_ATTESTED:
1294	                    event["mode"] = SYNC_MODE_ATTESTED
1295	                # Freeze the delivered summary when recovery could resolve it;
1296	                # records in snapshots older than the frozen-summary feature
1297	                # may not carry one, in which case the history query resolves
1298	                # live.
1299	                if rec.get("height") is not None:
1300	                    event["height"] = rec["height"]
1301	                    event["length"] = rec.get("length")
1302	                    event["status"] = rec.get("status")
1303	                audit_events.append(event)
1304	                covered[mode].add(identity)
1305	                count += 1
1306	            return count
1307	
1308	        return (
1309	            append_expiry(SYNC_MODE_PLAIN, expired_records)
1310	            + append_expiry(SYNC_MODE_ATTESTED, attested_expired_records)
1311	        )

1313	    @staticmethod
1314	    def _parse_persisted_trust_sources(
1315	        raw: object, path: str
1316	    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
1317	        """Strictly parse the persisted source-trust registry.
1318	
1319	        Unlike candidate forks (re-validated and silently dropped when stale),
1320	        the trust registry is authoritative configuration: a malformed entry
1321	        is snapshot corruption and fails recovery rather than being dropped.
1322	        Each record needs a non-empty source, a 64-char lowercase hex public
1323	        key, an integer expiry, a positive integer version and a known status.
1324	        """
1325	        if raw is None:
1326	            return {}
1327	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1328	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'trust_sources' must be a list")
1329	        sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
1330	        for entry in raw:
1331	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
1332	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source entry must be an object")
1333	            source = entry.get("source")
1334	            public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1335	            expires_at = entry.get("expires_at")
1336	            version = entry.get("version")
1337	            status = entry.get("status")
1338	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1339	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source must be a non-empty string")
1340	            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
1341	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1342	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has an invalid public_key"
1343	                )
1344	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
1345	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1346	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
1347	                )
1348	            if (
1349	                isinstance(version, bool)
1350	                or not isinstance(version, int)
1351	                or version < 1
1352	            ):
1353	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1354	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} version must be a positive integer"
1355	                )
1356	            if status not in (TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED):
1357	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1358	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has invalid status {status!r}"
1359	                )
1360	            if source in sources:
1361	                raise StateRecoveryError(
1362	                    path, f"duplicate trust source {source!r} in snapshot"
1363	                )
1364	            sources[source] = {
1365	                "public_key": public_key,
1366	                "expires_at": expires_at,
1367	                "version": version,
1368	                "status": status,
1369	            }
1370	        return sources

1390	    @staticmethod
1391	    def _parse_persisted_audit_events(raw: object, path: str) -> list[dict]:
1392	        """Strictly parse the append-only audit event log.
1393	
1394	        Every event is a JSON object carrying an integer ``at`` timestamp and a
1395	        string ``kind``; ``event_id`` values must be exactly 1..N with no gaps
1396	        or duplicates, since the id is the event's permanent audit position
1397	        (which also fixes the log's total ordering). Payload fields beyond
1398	        those three are retained verbatim.
1399	
1400	        The historical sync lifecycle events additionally have their provenance
1401	        metadata validated: ``sync_received`` / ``sync_adopted`` /
1402	        ``sync_expired`` must carry a non-empty ``source`` and ``request_id``
1403	        and a 64-char lowercase hex ``tip_hash``; an ``expires_at`` and the
1404	        frozen tip summary (``height`` / ``length`` / ``status``) are checked
1405	        when present — older snapshots' adopted events predate those fields, so
1406	        missing ones are accepted but malformed ones are corruption. The
1407	        keyless-allowlist events ``allowlist_added`` / ``allowlist_removed``
1408	        likewise require a non-empty ``source`` and an integer
1409	        ``expires_at``.
1410	        """
1411	        if raw is None:
1412	            return []
1413	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1414	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'audit_events' must be a list")
1415	        sync_kinds = {
1416	            EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED,
1417	            EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED,
1418	            EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
1419	        }
1420	        allowlist_kinds = {
1421	            EVENT_ALLOWLIST_ADDED,
1422	            EVENT_ALLOWLIST_REMOVED,
1423	        }
1424	        events: list[dict] = []
1425	        for i, event in enumerate(raw):
1426	            if not isinstance(event, dict):
1427	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {i + 1} must be an object")
1428	            event_id = event.get("event_id")
